about: measure contests of 2018 in Louisiana, in the layout of plan/PLAN.md section 3 with the fields data/README.md adds (D3). Built by pipeline/local_medsl.py from pipeline/intake/medsl_precinct.py's cache.

medsl.name: MIT Election Data and Science Lab, 2018 precinct-level returns, GitHub MEDSL/2018-elections-official at commit 42055b11dcd5
medsl.licence: no licence file in the repository; MEDSL's Dataverse sets of the same year are CC0 1.0
medsl.note: MEDSL's own earlier release, read by git (the repository now points to its Dataverse sets, which sit behind a guestbook; pipeline/intake/medsl_precinct.py --compare-dataverse matches the files by MD5); added up to the contest by pipeline/intake/medsl_precinct.py, files 2018-la-precinct-general.zip

model.name: the model's own forecast, method D3-v1.1
model.note: each year forecast from a fit on earlier years only; no polls are used

nara.name: National Archives, Electoral College Results (the sitting president's party)
nara.licence: US federal public record; no licence printed

klarner.name: Carl Klarner, State Legislative Election Returns, 1967-2022, Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/FJOGJB, v1.0, released 2024-06-12T21:56:14Z (the races route (a) is fitted on)

question.title: Ca No. 1 (Act 719 - Sb 31) - Prohibit Felon From Public Office

list.name: Louisiana Secretary of State: '2018 Proposed Constitutional Amendments, November 6, 2018 Election' (PDF, linked on the SOS 'Types of Elections' page as 'Nov. 6, 2018 Constitutional Amendments')

listed_statewide.quote: Proposed Amendment No. 1 Act 719 of the 2018 Regular Session of the Louisiana Legislature proposing to add Article I, Section 10.1 to the Louisiana Constitution.

fact.quote: Do you support an amendment to prohibit a convicted felon from seeking or holding public office or appointment within five years of completion of his sentence unless he is pardoned?
fact.why: the ballot question the state's list prints names no parish or municipality, and its subject reaches the whole state; the Act's own text was not read. Reading: not an amendment directly affecting not more than five parishes or five municipalities

notes: filed in MEDSL's local file with local offices (64 lines, one per county); the state's own list of that year's statewide measures names it, so its lines are joined into one statewide question (data/measure/statewide-filed-local.json)

threshold.rule: majority of electors voting on the amendment
threshold.quote: If a majority of the electors voting on the proposed amendment approve it, the governor shall proclaim its adoption, and it shall become part of this constitution, effective twenty days after the proclamation, unless the amendment provides otherwise.
threshold.matched: by the type the source's title states (amendment); the state's list of its statewide measures shows it is not an amendment directly affecting not more than five parishes or five municipalities [inferred] (data/measure/statewide-filed-local.json)

p.not_computed: fewer than 100 like measures in earlier years in the sources taken in (95) for the class 'statewide measure'
